title: Late-night GPU throttle oddities - worklog
content:
Summary

Quick notes from the late-night on-call window (11/17 -> 11/18) — cluster: dedicated-gpu-west-2, pool: ded-capacity-4

What happened (high level)
- Intermittent, high tail-latency and throughput regressions on ded-capacity-4 between 23:40–02:10 UTC.
- Symptoms: token throughput drops ~40-70% on affected nodes, per-request latency spikes from median 42ms to 180–700ms, sustained for 3–6 minutes then sometimes recovering.
- Prometheus/Exporters show periodic GPU utilization drops while CPU utilization remains high on the same nodes. NVML exported metrics show active kernels present but SM utilization oscillating.
- Autoscaler reacted poorly — attempted to scale down some low-util instances because node-level CPU looked low, while actual GPU processes were congested. This caused transient placement pressure and more tail latency.

Initial hypotheses (ranked)
1) Noisy neighbor causing PCIe contention or MIG share interference (multi-job colliding on PCI bandwidth).
2) Driver/runtime mismatch + power cap enforcement (recent driver push two days ago).
3) Autoscaler threshold units misconfigured (scale-down uses cpu_percent but should consider gpu_busy).
4) KV cache or serving runtime bug: continuous batcher occasionally serializes unexpectedly when queue depth crosses boundary.
5) Hardware thermal/protection flashing (one node reported transient ECC warnings in dmesg).

Evidence collected (commands / graphs)
- top / htop snapshots (see gist link in linked_artifacts) show model processes present, CPU at 35-55% but io wait spikes.
- nvidia-smi stats during event: GPU utilization oscillating 5-98%, memory stable; persisted CUDA kernel counts high.
- dmesg excerpt: "NVML: GPU 2 ECC error resolved" (timestamped at 23:54) — ambiguous.
- perf counters from one node: PCIe bandwidth inbound saturations concurrent with GPU utilization drop.
- Grafana panels: per-node token rate vs GPU util shows anti-correlation; block device metrics normal.
- Autoscaler logs: scaleDown.decider triggered because node_cpu_pct < 20 for 3m on 2025-11-18T00:12Z.

Immediate mitigations applied during window
- Temporarily disabled aggressive scale-down policy (rolled back commit from infra PR #281) at 00:25 UTC — prevented further thrashing.
- Tainted two suspect nodes (ded-gn-04, ded-gn-11) and drained model pods to isolate; latency stabilized on remaining pool.
- Forcing driver module reload on ded-gn-11 (rmmod nvidia; modprobe nvidia) after draining; brief improvement but not definitive.

Playbook draft (for next time)
1) Detection rules (alerting):
   - New alert: GPU_utilization_anti_correlation: fire when per-node token_rate decreases by >30% while GPU_utilization decreases by >40% in the same 2-minute window AND pcie_tx_bytes_rate increases >25%.
   - Alert severity: P1 if >2 nodes in same AZ affected, otherwise P2.
2) Triage checklist (quick steps):
   a) Capture: kubectl top / pod metrics, nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,clocks.current,temperature --loop-ms=500 for 60s.
   b) Check node dmesg for ECC/PCIe errors, journalctl -u nvidia*, and /var/log/messages.
   c) Query Prometheus: rate(gpu_compute_time[1m]) vs rate(request_tokens[1m]) and pcie_tx_bytes_total.
   d) If PCIe congestion suspected -> cordon + drain node, run pci-rescan and check firmware versions.
   e) If driver mismatch suspected -> reference device-driver-matrix in Confluence and run remote repro on isolated node.
3) Autoscaler safety knobs:
   - Prefer scale-to-zero only after confirming gpu_busy_pct < 10 for 10m AND node_request_queue_depth == 0.
   - Add gpu_busy_pct metric to ScaleDownDecider; fallback to current behavior if missing.
4) Isolation strategy for noisy neighbor (fast):
   - Apply a temporary cgroup CPU limit for non-model processes, or move suspect low-priority jobs to separate node pool.
   - Enable MIG partitioning for heavy multi-tenant nodes where supported.

Unresolved details / experiments to run
- Reproduce under load: create synthetic workload with heavy small micro-batches to attempt to trigger the oscillation pattern (aim to hit PCIe saturation). Riya volunteered to run this in a staging pool.
- Validate whether the autoscaler mis-trigger correlates with the same metric window on other pools (query window: 00:00–01:30).
- Confirm driver rollback experiment: validate if older NVIDIA driver (from 2025-11-10) removes oscillation. Planned test on ded-staging-1.
- Check node firmware/chipset revisions: two affected nodes show older uCode; schedule maintenance if mismatch found.

Operators notes (things I did that helped / didn't help)
- Taint+drain is effective and quick for customer impact mitigation.
- Reboot of node (cold) was not attempted during the incident — feared disruption to long-running jobs — will consider for follow-up if we find a hardware/firmware cause.
- Driver reload sometimes restored utilization for ~5-10 minutes then regress. Points to either power/thermal protective behavior or a kernel-space resource leak.
- Setting autoscaler to ignore short CPU dips saved us from repeated churn.

Follow-ups (owners)
- Riya: orchestrate staging repro and run the synthetic PCIe-saturation test (target date: 2025-11-21).
- Luis: add gpu_busy_pct into scaleDownDecider and ship small safety gate (PR opened) (target: 2025-11-20).
- Samir: schedule firmware audit for ded-capacity-4 nodes and follow through with vendor if needed (target: 2025-11-24).
- Maya (me): draft post-incident runbook page and summary for oncall rotation; include quick triage checklist and Grafana playbooks (due: 2025-11-22).

Open questions / unknowns
- Is this unique to our kernel/NVIDIA driver combo or an application pattern (batching + kv cache) that only surfaces under certain request shapes?
- Are GPU power-management/pState changes being triggered by thermal headroom logic? Need better telemetry of powercap/pstate events.
- Can we get more granular PCIe telemetry (per-lane) from vendor?

Notes to self (informal)
- Add example PromQL snippets into runbook: e.g. 
  - rate(request_tokens[1m]) / sum by(node)(rate(gpu_compute_time[1m]))  -> tokens-per-gpu-second
  - (increase(node_pcie_tx_bytes_total[5m]) > 0) && (avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[2m]) < 30)
- Slack threads: #sre-dedicated (thread t12345) has raw logs and timestamped screenshots.
- Keep this doc light and messy - we'll formalize in Confluence once hypotheses narrowed.

Appendix: useful commands (copy/paste)
- kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=ded-gn-11
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm --format=csv -l 0.5
- sudo journalctl -k | grep -i nvidia | tail -n 200
- sudo cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/power_dpm_state || echo "no-power-dpm"

End of late-night worklog.

-- Maya
